en: Xingguo Zeng, whose style name was Xiugang, was the successor to Zhengzong Xinyin.
He was the son of the Fang family from the region of Min. Having entered the monastic life in his childhood, he possessed natural intelligence;
his learning required no further deliberation. He treated the assembly with respect and served his teacher with propriety. One day, the teacher saw him and asked:
"Yesterday you were ill; the assembly said you were about to die. What was your thought on this? He replied, "Originally there is no birth; how could there be death?
The Master said, "Since you know there is no birth, from where have you come? (Guozeng) raised his voice and recited the Buddha’s name.
The Master asked, "Where have you gone? (The monk) placed his hands over his chest and remained silent for a long while. The Master asked, "What is the matter therein?
He immediately replied with a verse: "The fundamental, pure essence is as it is; It manifests skillfully according to conditions, whether square or round.
Turning the light back upon itself transcends past and present; Truly wondrous and pervasive, it is beyond words. The Master said, "So it is, so it is."

"It is so. You should naturally reach the state of purity. He then entrusted him with a verse: "The opportune moment is directly pointed out at Xiugang: The essence is revealed as true permanence, not concealed.
I now entrust this to you; you should cherish it. When the time comes, you must follow the ancestral transmission."
The monk De-yuan’s Dharma name was Mingjing. He was the son of the Shi family from Fucing County. Yu-cheng went to visit him to seek and request the essential truth.
The Master said, "Our Buddha, in his great compassion and impartiality, expounded the Three Vehicles and Five Teachings to deliver beings according to their capacities.

At the end, he held up a flower to show the assembly, transmitting the separate tradition outside the teachings—the wondrous mind of Nirvana, the true mark which is markless. He then entrusted [the teaching].
The patriarch Mahākāśyapa transmitted it in succession until it reached Master Bodhidharma, who came to this eastern land.

He pointed directly at the human mind, so that one may see one’s nature and become a Buddha. You must personally turn the light back upon yourself and reflect within; thus clarify your own fundamental mind and perceive your own original nature.
Neither form nor emptiness; neither middle nor outside. It penetrates thoroughly the ten directions and harmonizes the three periods of time.
The hundred thousand samādhis and the wondrous functions as numerous as the sands of the Ganges do not depart from this very place. (Dequan had an awakening) and immediately spoke a verse:

"Originally pure and inconceivable, Adapting to circumstances and becoming perfect according to the occasion. Samādhi manifests before one, penetrating the Great Way; Light is emitted and auspicious signs appear."

How wondrous and marvelous! The Master said: "You must personally uphold it. He bestowed a verse of entrustment concerning the Perfectly Enlightened Seed-Wisdom, the single transmission of the direct pointing to the mind-seal of the mind:
"The True Suchness, formless, manifests brilliant clarity; I entrust this to you, O Lord of the East, that you may preserve it well.
The time has come for the era of compassion to receive future generations."
Sengguo Jian, whose Dharma name was Tiandong, was the son of the Pan family of the Three Mountains. He sought a teacher to realize the ultimate Way of True Permanence.
The Master held up one finger and pointed to it, saying, "Do you understand? (Guojian) performed a prostration. The Master said, "I have no Dharma to give to others.
If you can cease all external conditions and do not cling to the view of emptiness, turn the light back to reflect within and see your own [nature]."
"The nature of the mind must be understood. (Guojian) suddenly attained realization and spoke this verse: "Originally there is no obstruction; Pure and eternally sovereign.

The Unmoving Honored One of Suchness Manifests the dharma-realm within his luminous eye. The Master said, "If you maintain this as it is, it will reach the state of pure, true, and wondrous excellence.
He further entrusted him with another verse: "Silently and completely uphold the true command; A single branch [spreads] into five."

"Leaves fall to meet those who understand; the fragrance of the lineage continues through the succession of the most worthy sages. I entrust you: at this time, you must cause the ancestral temple to shine.
The monk De-fa, whose Dharma name is Yuejiang, was the son of the Chen family of Min County. He requested instruction on the ritual matters concerning the three bodies of the Buddha:
the Dharmakāya, the Saṃbhogakāya, and the Nirmāṇakāya. The Master said: "Do not seek it outwardly. You yourself possess the perfectly luminous nature of awakening; its wondrous function is manifest."

Before [this realization], essence and function were not partial; fruit and flower were manifested together. The three contemplations were harmoniously integrated, and the ten directions were vast and transparent.

Spanning from antiquity to the present, there was neither deficiency nor excess. (Dehong) Suddenly experiencing a profound awakening, he spoke this verse: "The original nature is profoundly still, its essence is suchness (*tathatā*);

Its wondrous function extends in all directions, freely rolling up or unfolding. The enlightened nature is empty and mysterious, originally without form; Skillful means and ultimate reality are both fused."
"It should be inexhaustible. The Master then gave his seal of approval, saying, "Support yourself well. He further entrusted him with a verse: "Grasping a single branch, it manifests in full majesty;
Through the meeting of past affinities, it is bestowed upon Yuejiang. I entrust you, a man of talent, to cherish this; When the time comes, propagate the Dharma and repay the Patriarchs' kindness."
This man, whose name is Wonhyeon (圓暕) and whose style-name is Dongam (洞庵), is the son of the Tu family of Qin-chuan in Zhuji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang.
He came seeking the direct pointing to supreme Bodhi. The Master asked, "What is the matter of daily life?
Wonhyeon replied, "The pure breeze is surely in my hand. The Master asked, "What is the unimpeded nature of reality? Wonhyeon folded his hands.
[The Master] struck him on the chest. After remaining silent for a long while, the Master asked, "What is the non-obstruction of principle and phenomena?

He replied, "Everywhere one penetrates the capital. The Master immediately granted his approval, saying, "Take good care of yourself. He further entrusted him with a verse: "Principle and phenomena are distinct;
named Dong'an, They are harmoniously integrated, unobstructed, and vast in capacity. I now entrust you with nothing further; The time has come to continue the flame."
Baoling Shan. Sengguo Yan was styled Shouyue; he was the son of the Wei family from Guizhou County in Shaowu Prefecture. He requested instruction on the causal conditions of the Great Matter.
The Master said, "The banyan tree in front of the gate is always like spring. (Guo Yan) hesitated, and the Master immediately shouted. Yan...
He prostrated himself. The Master asked, "Do you understand? Guoyan replied, "I do not yet comprehend its meaning; I hope the Master will grant me an instruction.

The Master said, "The Great Matter is not obtained from without. You should, at all times, remain undeluded in every thought-moment. Let the true mind always abide, flowing freely without obstruction.
When the nature of awakening is all-pervasive, there is neither lack nor excess. Guoyan attained a realization and immediately spoke this verse: [Verse omitted as per instructions]
[The Master] said: "Profoundly still and naturally so, it responds to the great chiliocosm; for those who meet the occasion, the wondrous mystery is uniquely revealed.

Perfectly luminous and unimpeded, it transcends past and present; penetrating and all-illuminating, it shines through the nightless sky. The Teacher said: "Since you have realized this, you should cherish it.

Furthermore, I entrust you with this verse: "The single flower of Shaolin became five petals on the lotus; Transmitted down to the present, it reveals the fruit and extends [the lineage]. To the heroic spirits, suddenly..."
The Provincial Governor received this instruction. Without leaving his current location, he beheld the Jetavana Grove.
Sengguo, whose dharma name was Biyun, was the son of the Peng family from Min County in Fuzhou. Upon meeting the Master, he asked:

"What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Do you understand? Guoxiang replied, "I hope you will grant me your compassion. The Master said, "To suddenly awaken to one's own nature is to be the true, heavenly Buddha.
Otherwise, it is merely a waste of labor. If you are a Chan practitioner who truly investigates and genuinely awakens, you must realize it before words;
this is the fundamental style of our house—it does not belong to existence or non-existence, nor is it concerned with sound or form."
All things are fully manifest; they appear clearly at every turn. Picked up with the hand as it reaches out, there is nothing that is not so.
Buddhas and sentient beings are fundamentally equal. (Guo Xiang) attained a realization and said, "Originally, this is one's own. The Master asked, "What is 'one's own'?
(Xiang) recited the Buddha’s name once. The Master asked, "What is the Buddha? (Xiang) folded his hands and remained silent. The Master then—

[The Master] gave his seal of approval. "It is fitting that you attain true sincerity. He further entrusted him with two verses: "The intent of 'settling the mind' before the emerald cliff of the Patriarch, Was transmitted to Caoxi and revealed universally.
This succession continues like a blazing flame down to the present day; At this time of entrustment, you should uphold the principles of the Patriarchs."
The monk Mingzhi, whose style name was Dasheng, was the son of Zhou Shihaicai of Zhuhai in Zhuji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang Province.
He went to seek certification from the Master. The Master asked, "Who is your teacher? He replied, "Baofeng. The Master asked, "What did he teach you to do?
He replied, "To contemplate the mind and recite the Buddha’s name. The Master asked, "What is the mind? Mingzhi held up his rosary.

The Master asked, "What is the Buddha? [The student] simply stood there with his hands folded. The Master gave his seal of approval, saying, "Take good care of yourself. He further entrusted him with a verse:
"Expedient means and ultimate truth both revealed, this is called the Great Vehicle; Realizing the unborn, its radiance shines through ancient and modern times.
Entrusting you, O brilliant spirit, you must cherish this well; When the time comes, you must instruct those who follow."
The monk Dezong was styled Guxin. He was the son of the Zheng family from Minnan. Seeking the essential truth of his teacher, the Master said:

"In our school, there is fundamentally no verbal teaching, nor is there any dharma to be given to others. You need only, throughout the twelve periods of the day and within the four modes of deportment, turn the light inward to reflect back, gathering delusions to return to the true, clarifying your own original mind and seeing your own original nature. Do not let even a hair’s breadth [of distraction] intervene."
He had been somewhat dim-witted, but now he understood with vivid clarity. (Emperor Dezong) suddenly attained realization and spoke this verse:
"The fundamental nature is profoundly still and thus; How can its wondrous function be measured? It fills the great trichiliocosm, Manifesting the true and eternal wherever it appears.

The Master immediately certified him, saying, "You must take care of yourself. He further entrusted him with another verse: "The Mind-Seal of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, from antiquity to the present, Is directly revealed when the occasion arises."
This is most clear. I entrust you, O worthy one, to guard this well. At that time, you shall continue the ancestral flame to receive future generations.
The monk named Deguang, whose style name was Chekong, was the son of the Yang family from Changshu County in Suzhou Prefecture.

He went to seek certification [of his realization], and the Master asked: "What instructions did the various masters give you? He replied: "They all instructed me to recite the Buddha’s name. The Master asked: "How so?"
"This is the Buddha. (De Guang) joined his palms at his chest and asked, "What is the matter that manifests when the occasion arises? (Guang) recited the name of the Buddha once.

The Master immediately granted him approval, saying, "You should maintain this yourself," and further entrusted him with a verse: "Reciting the Buddha's name, one suddenly awakens to the original cause;
At all times, one does not depart from this very person. Diligently nurture the state of pure sincerity; When the flame continues, it shall be the time [of realization]."
Sengguo Tong, whose Dharma name was Dacheng, succeeded to the ancestral hall. He was the son of the Wang family from Changle County in Fuzhou.
Seeking a teacher to point directly to the meaning of the West, he asked Master Cuoshan, who said, "What is it? Sengguo Tong replied, "I do not understand; I beg you to grant me instruction."
The Master said, "Go for now. Tong said, "I hope you will grant me your compassion for my poverty. The Master said, "Do not follow after sounds;

do not be deceived by forms. Do not debate existence and non-existence; do not distinguish between east and west. Simply awaken for yourself: right where you are is True Suchness—tranquil, vast, and penetrating."
"Wondrously bright and sovereign—do you understand? Tong suddenly attained realization upon these words and immediately spoke a verse:
"Suchness is unmoving, like empty space; Manifesting without restriction, penetrating everywhere. Existence and non-existence are not established; subject and object are exhausted."

Form and emptiness are non-dual, perfectly interfused. The Master granted his seal of approval, saying, "Maintain this well yourself. He further entrusted him with a verse: "The Dharma rain of Nanhua falls everywhere as grace;
The mind-seal is transmitted to continue the ancestral lamp. Through past affinities we have fortunately met; you should hold this in high esteem."

At that time, there was one named Xu Yan-yao (Continuing Flame Radiance), who belonged to the lineage of the Zhengzong (Orthodox Lineage). He was the son of the Li family from Dagou County in Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi.
Having gone to seek instruction, the Master asked, "How is your daily life during the present moment? He replied, "I constantly recite the Buddha's name. The Master said—
[The student] asked, "What is the Buddha? He replied, "The mind is it. The Master asked, "What is the mind? He replied, "The Buddha is the mind. Then he spoke this verse:
"The One Truth alone reveals the gate of non-duality; Mind is Buddha, and principle and phenomena are fused.

Body and function are both manifest; now we have fortunately met. Originally pure, reaching the state of no-remainder. The Master then gave him his seal of approval, saying, "You should always remain thus."

Furthermore, he entrusted him with another verse: "The great matter and its causal conditions reveal both essence and function; In movement and stillness, skillful and pure is the fragrance of Prajñā.
Pervading and harmonizing the Dharma-realm, it is eternally unimpeded; The perfect, luminous, seed-like wisdom realizes the true and eternal."
Sengguo, whose dharma name was Daida, was the son of the Chen family of the Three Mountains. With reverent sincerity, he paid his respects and requested the Master’s instruction.

The Master said: "It is originally complete and perfect; it is not obtained from others. You should turn the light back upon yourself to reflect, thereby clarifying your own fundamental mind and seeing your own original nature.
It is neither form nor sound; it is neither empty nor existent. It pervades the ten directions and is all-penetrating."
"The three periods have been complete from the very beginning; have you ever known this? (Guoqing) then spoke a verse: "Subtle brilliance clearly reveals the True Doctrine;
Essence and function are impartial, possessing perfect fusion. Densely and without interval is Avalokiteśvara; Unmoving in suchness, he manifests spiritual penetration.
The Master said, "Excellent! You have done well. He further entrusted him with another verse: "Beyond the kalpas, the spiritual branch is free from even a speck of dust."
"Seizing whatever comes to hand, I show it to all people; those of brilliant talent suddenly awaken and inherit this intent. I entrust you to propagate the ancestral temple when the time is right.
The monk Guo Kui, whose Dharma name is Dazhou, is the son of the Zheng family of the Three Mountains. He requested instruction on the causal conditions of the Great Matter.
The Master said, "Come forward. Guo Kui stepped forward. The Master asked, "Is this great, or is it small? He replied, "I do not yet understand this meaning.
The Master said, "If one possesses superior faculties and sharp intelligence, upon seeing and hearing this instruction, they will be able to awaken and enter [the Way].

If this is not yet the case, you should naturally exert yourself, studying with single-minded sincerity. Suddenly, the clouds of delusion will be dispersed, and the moon of the mind will become perfectly bright."
Only then did he realize that he himself had a great matter, which was equal to that of the Buddha and without distinction. Guo Kui then said, "Originally, it is fully possessed.
The Master asked, "What is it that is originally so? He replied, "Originally, there is neither movement nor stillness; it comes forth to respond to the ten directions. The Master said:
This essential point has long been kept in silence until now, reaching its ultimate purity. He further entrusted a verse, stating: "The final stroke was bestowed upon Kāśyapa;

it has been transmitted from India to this land of the East. Worthy and spirited practitioners must awaken to and enter into it; when karmic conditions and capacities accord, one may join the lineage of the fragrant flowers."
The monk Dejian, whose dharma name was Dayong, was the son of the Wang family from Min County. He sought a teacher for certification. The master asked, "Whom have you seen before?
He replied, "Master Tianzhen. The master asked, "What did he teach you? He replied, "He taught me to investigate *nianfo* (the recitation of the Buddha's name).
The master asked, "Who is it that investigates? Dejian held up one finger. The master asked, "How is this?"
"This is the Buddha. (Jian) joined his palms for a long time and spoke in verse: "Neither going nor coming—wondrous within the wondrous; Solely maintaining a single thought, subtle and continuous.
Suddenly and abruptly awakening to the principle of non-arising, One breaks through empty space without using a fist.
The Master asked, "With what do you break through empty space? (Jian) called out the Buddha’s name in a loud voice. The Master then gave him his seal of approval, saying, "Protect yourself well."
Reverently, I further offer this verse: The bright mirror is not the stand; its radiance spans past and present. The wind of the school spreads far and wide, transmitted one after another.
From now on, the entrustment is complete with no further concerns; He conceals his traces in true purity to receive future generations.
Sengguo, whose Dharma name was Tianzhang, was the son of the Han family of the Three Mountains.

He sought a teacher to reach the ultimate realization of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, for they appear in the world solely for the sake of this one great matter. The Master said, "What kind of causal condition is it that you are asking about right now?
(Cóng) suddenly attained a realization upon these words and immediately said, "It turns out that, fundamentally, I am no different from the Buddhas and Patriarchs."

"How marvelous! He then spoke a verse, saying: 'The Dharma-nature is originally without marks; by thus awakening, one accords with the True Source. Its wondrous function pervades the sands of the world; there is nowhere it is not perfectly penetrating.
The Master then granted him approval, entrusting him with True Purity. He further instructed him with another verse: 'The direct pointing of the single transmission reveals the original source;
transmitted through successive generations, it is the gate of non-duality. Entrust this to you, O talented one, and you should hold it in deep respect. At that time...
"May you illuminate your ancestors and continue the succession of the fragrant [Dharma] lineage.
The monk Yuanshou, whose Dharma name was Letao, was the son of the Su family from Luyi County in Guide Prefecture, Henan.

Having admired the Master’s reputation, he went to attend him, seeking the seal of the Teacher’s Dharma. The Master said, "The seal of the Dharma is not non-existent; it is not obtained from without. However, do not..."
Following after sounds and forms, one becomes obstructed by names and phrases; yet this is perfectly clear and distinct, inherently possessed by every person.

Its majestic spirit is vast and penetrating, seeking it through kalpas one finds it indestructible. It accompanies us without ever departing—how could it not be realized? (Yuan Shou) Suddenly, upon these words, he attained realization.

Having realized the fundamental source, he spoke this verse: "The original nature is suchness; It is neither form nor sound. The Three Mysteries are one in ultimate rest; Profoundly still, it is the self-sovereign truth.
The Master said, "Maintain this in such a manner, refining and polishing it until it shines with clarity. He further entrusted him with another verse:
Caoshui has universally revealed this to all who know; the seal of the orthodox mind connects with those of superior capacity. This transmitted principle should be held in reverence;
when the time comes, one must surely receive the extraordinary successor.

Sengguo’s courtesy name was Tianjian. He was the son of the Xu family of Min County. Seeking a teacher for the essentials of the True and Right, the Master [Fayan] remained silent for a long while and then asked, "Do you understand?
Sengguo replied, "I do not understand. The Master said, "The Right means being without partiality; the True means being without falsehood.

The Essential is to attain awakening through faith and understanding, thereby entering the gate of the Dharma-realm. Through precept, concentration, and wisdom, one pursues the profound path to the Land of Bliss. You should turn toward this."

At all times, relinquish all external conditions. When the nature of one’s own mind is clear and not deluded by even a hair’s breadth, and when essence and function are perfectly interfused, only then will one know that the Great Way is inherently complete from the beginning.
(Qing) immediately attained realization upon hearing these words and spoke this verse:

"The King of the Dharma of Suchness, His radiance illuminates the ten directions. Perfectly interfused and wondrous beyond compare, In true emptiness, there is neither annihilation nor permanence. The Master then conferred his seal of approval.
"Very well. Take good care of yourself and uphold [the Dharma] with diligence. (And so forth. He further entrusted him with a verse:

"The True Edict of the Dharma King, from antiquity to the present, Has been successively inherited by those of noble spirit who attained sudden enlightenment. I now seal you to continue this succession of fragrant flowers; When the time comes, you must instruct future generations.
Seng Mingyu, whose style name was Wuxia, was the son of the Chen family from Jiahe County in Heduan Prefecture, Beijing. He went to seek instruction...
Regarding the Master, he sought the essential points of the Dharma with single-minded resolve. The Master sat upon his seat and looked at him, asking, "Do you understand?
He replied, "I have not yet grasped this meaning. The Master said, "The Ultimate Way pervades all under heaven; it is not the case that it is incomplete in any single person.

It is simply that you must examine and awaken to it from time to time, and maintain its presence at every moment. Your own mind-nature—how does it differ from that of the ancient sages? From this point forward, enter through awakening and expand it widely."
Zizai (Mingyu) suddenly attained sudden enlightenment and immediately spoke this verse: “True Suchness is fundamentally serene; its manifestations pervade the great trichiliocosm.

Profoundly still and eternally pure, the provisional and the real are mysteriously unified within its essence. The Master confirmed that it was indeed so: “It is supremely pure, subtle, and wondrous.”

He further entrusted them with a verse: "The True Dharma and the Mind-Seal are the Gate of Non-duality. Directly pointing to the capacity of the recipient to realize the original source, I entrust this to you, O gifted one;
you should cherish it well. When the time comes, you must teach and transmit it as the Patriarchs did."
Sengguo, whose dharma name was Tianji, was the son of the Ruan family of Min County.

He sought instruction from Chan Master Da’an, entering the master’s room with reverence and sincerity to seek the teacher’s essential truth. The Master sat upright and displayed it to him with total ease, then asked, "Do you understand?"

The disciple replied, "I pray that you will grant me your compassionate instruction. The Master said, "If you are a true practitioner, you should let go of all external conditions and maintain a single thought-moment alone.

Be mindful of this and dwell in it. When the nature of this mindfulness is like empty space and the mind is like the great earth, with the sun of wisdom and the moon of insight penetrating through to perfect clarity, you will finally know that the Great Way is inherently complete from the beginningless past to the endless future—what could be added and what could be diminished?"

[The Master] reduced [the number of disciples]. (Teng) attained realization upon hearing these words and immediately spoke a verse: "The fundamental essence is originally without form; Suchness is constantly manifest before us.
It has never ceased throughout past and present; Its wondrous responsiveness is boundless. The Master’s seal of approval accorded with his inner realization.

He was instructed to maintain this state well. Furthermore, a verse was entrusted to him: "The Great Way is majestic, spanning past and present; Once awakened, it manifests within the person here and now. This charge is entrusted to the worthy and the sage."
"You should cherish this. When the time comes, you shall join the ranks of the illustrious to bring glory to the ancestral temple.
The Master's name was Guorong, his style name Jingqi, and he was the son of the Chen family from Nanping County in Yanping Prefecture.

He sought a teacher to bestow upon him the essential points of the Dharma. The Master said: "Take the mind as the fundamental principle and awakening as the standard. The wondrous substance of true emptiness is inherently..."

Spontaneously natural, it belongs neither to existence nor non-existence; fundamentally, it is neither movement nor stillness. It penetrates the profound source of the ages and establishes the patterns for the myriad phenomena.
When the kalpa-fire destroys all things, it remains eternally serene; when the Dharma is about to vanish, its entire body is revealed. A single ray of numinous light.

"It has been complete from the beginning; it does not decrease among ordinary beings, nor does it increase among sages. It simply requires that you neither harbor hatred nor attachment, and you will see through it with clear, luminous understanding.

Upon hearing this, Rong suddenly attained a realization and immediately presented a verse, saying: "Originally such as it is, it is bright and pure; Formless and nameless, it is penetratingly perfect and luminous.
Pervading the entire realm of sand-grains, it is fused and unimpeded; Neither defiled nor pure, its awakening is empty and spiritual. The Master (Zhaozhou) certified his realization.

"Indeed. Preserve your essence with purity. Furthermore, I entrust you with this verse: A single letter that accords with the occasion seals True Suchness; Only then can one believe that the Way of Non-arising is not in vain.
The three truths are perfectly integrated without obstruction; I entrust you to inherit the path of the Patriarchs at this time."
Sengguo Man was a man of natural talent whose Dharma name was Tianzi. He was the son of the Ye family of Min County.
Having requested instruction from Chan Master Da’an, he paid his respects and asked the Master, “What is this great causal condition that has appeared in the world?

The Master said, “Come forward. (Man) took a step forward. The Master asked, “Do you understand? He replied, “I do not know; please grant me your compassionate instruction. The Master said, “The Original...”
Coming is neither two nor three; let the one who meets the occasion look as they will. This is the ritual of all Buddhas, the true Dharma-eye of the patriarchs.
Encountering the conditions, it is directly revealed; upon awakening and entering, the ocean of nature is vast. Perfectly interfused and without obstruction, pure and serene, free from waves.

(Full) Under these words, the sky of nature becomes expansive and the ground of the mind opens with clarity. Thereupon, he spoke this verse: "Stands alone, majestically manifest, throughout antiquity."

"Now, the realization of signlessness and quiescence is perfectly luminous; it pervades the ten directions and penetrates the three truths. On the ground of the reality-limit, not even a speck of dust remains.
The Master then granted him certification, saying, "Guard and uphold this well. He further entrusted him with a verse: "The mind-seal of the Buddhas and Patriarchs was personally transmitted;
From lamp to lamp, the flame has continued until this day. You, a worthy and brilliant recipient, should honor it with respect; When the time and conditions arrive, awakening will dawn."
The successor was Sengguo, whose current dharma name is Bensheng. He was the second son of the Han family of Qianbing in Wucheng, Min Province.

He sought further instruction from Chan Master Zhankong and visited the master to request an exposition of the essential points of the Dharma. The master stared directly at him for a long time, then asked:
He asked, "Do you understand? (Xian) suddenly attained realization and spoke this verse: "Suchness is unmoving, fundamentally empty yet luminous;

Manifestations appear in harmony, pervading every mote of dust in all lands. Sudden awakening to non-arising transcends the Dharma-realm; Adapting to circumstances while remaining perfect, one realizes true clarity."

The Master’s seal is likewise so. Guard well its purity and essence. He further entrusted him with a verse: "The mind transmitted outside the teachings since ancient times, Patriarch after patriarch, their fragrance linked as they successively inherited it.
I now entrust it to you; you should cherish it, So that lamp after lamp continues the flame, illuminating the ancestral hall."
Sengguo Run, whose Dharma name was Tianjin, was the son of the Jiang family of Min County. He sought instruction from Chan Master Da’an, approaching the master to inquire:
“What is the Way of true correctness? The master pointed upward with his finger. He asked, “Do you understand? He replied, “I do not know.
The master said, “If you truly seek the Way, you should, in the midst of time, not dwell upon states of achievement. Do not...”
Chasing after sounds and forms, one must understand the fundamental nature of the mind. Keep this in mind at all times;

when it becomes vast and transparently penetrating, only then will you know that the Great Way is neither obstructed nor blocked—level, open, and composed. It is a state of leisurely ease, like being in the presence of Maitreya.

(Rùn) Suddenly, upon these words, he attained realization and spoke this verse: "The wondrous, void, and numinous is ever-present throughout past and present. The skillful means of perfect integration reside within the person."
The entirety of True Suchness gives birth to the sun of wisdom; returning to the root and source, one is fundamentally pure. The Master said:

"If you can thus take up the task well and cultivate it with refined purity, I shall further entrust you with this verse: 'In true emptiness there is neither going nor coming; It cannot be squeezed into a ball, nor can it be pushed apart.
Through the convergence of past conditions, you have received this intent; I entrust you now to receive the future talent.'"
Sengguo, whose Dharma name was Hui’an, was the son of the Xue family of Fuqing County. He paid his respects to the Master and requested instruction on supreme bodhi. The Master said:

"The supreme and wondrous Way is fundamentally beyond words and speech, and possesses neither names nor forms. It is numinous clarity without abiding, utterly transcending the sense organs and their objects.
Pure and complete without remainder, it is pervasive, harmonious, and sovereign. This is what you inherently possess; it does not come from without."
He attained realization (*kǒngmiè*). Suddenly, having an awakening, he spoke this verse: "Bodhi is originally and fundamentally empty yet luminous; At every moment, it manifests great radiance.
True Suchness (*tathatā*) is vast and penetrating throughout the Dharma-realm; Pure and harmonious, it shines through past and present.

The Master then certified him, saying, "Support yourself well. He further entrusted him with a verse: "The Dharma-seal of the Buddhas and Patriarchs points directly to the mind; Thoroughly awaken to it."
The lineage was transmitted down to Guo Ming. Cherish and nurture the pure and true blossoms. When the time comes, employ compassion to continue the ancestral temple.
The monk Yuanjing, whose dharma name is Wukong, is a son of the Chen family from Changle County.

He received his training under Chan Master Wuda and sought further instruction from Chan Master Zhenkong. One day he came to pay his respects and immediately presented this verse: "Fundamentally there is none..."
"Departure is also without coming. He emitted light and manifested auspicious omens, secretly revealing [the truth]. "Profoundly still and pure, beyond compare;
illuminating heaven and earth, utterly free from a speck of dust. The Master asked, "What is this that illuminates? [Jing] extended one hand. The Master said:
"What is the place of purity? [The student] folded his hands at his chest and remained silent for a long while. The Master said, "So it is, so it is. Nurture the true and pure.
He further entrusted him with a verse: "The flower held up for the assembly is spring beyond kalpas; Awakening to the nature of mind reveals our original sameness.
The descendants of the Patriarchs shall join in the fragrance of this intent; I entrust you to uphold the ancient wind when the time comes."
The Sengzheng Yuan, whose courtesy name was Zhongtian, was the son of the Chen family from Huian County in Quanzhou Prefecture. He requested instruction from Chan Master Dagan.
One day, upon seeing the Master, he bowed and asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "Do you understand? He replied, "I have not yet attained realization;
I beg you to grant me your guidance. The Master said, "The Buddha is your own mind; there is no need to seek it elsewhere. The nature of the mind is in profound accord [with reality]."

Without self and without person, the fundamental reality is revealed alone. It has been perfectly accomplished from the beginning. (Yuan) Suddenly, upon hearing these words, he attained realization and spoke this verse:

"Through vast eons I have wandered until this very day; I am grateful to my teacher for directly pointing out the original cause. Suddenly I have reached the true and eternal, uninterrupted and seamless;
To follow the square and become round depends entirely upon the person. The Master said: "Such as this, you should head toward the deep mountain peaks."
The site is a place of ancient traces, pure and serene, where one nurtures the true and simple. He further entrusted me with a verse: "Lamp after lamp continues the flame until perfect fullness;

suddenly one awakens to how essence and function are fundamentally both complete. Entrust this to worthy talent for proper preservation; when the time comes for sorrowful awakening, emulate the ancestral transmission."
Sengyuanjin, styled Wuhuai, was the son of the Xue family from Fucing County. He received his formal training under Chan Master Chekong and sought further instruction from Chan Master Zhankong.
He requested the master’s guidance regarding the great matter of life and death. The master said: "Look! Look! Look! For one who understands, it is not difficult to see.
It is not obtained from the outside, nor does it reside within. Simply turn your light back upon yourself and you will realize it."

Delusive thoughts are severed; from the beginning, there is only the single reality—neither two nor three. (Upon hearing these words), he suddenly attained realization and immediately spoke this verse:
"True Suchness is fundamentally formless; Pure and stainless, it is free from even a speck of dust. I dedicate myself to the treasury of the unconditioned, Releasing forth a great radiance.

The Master confirmed that his realization was thus and instructed him to nurture it with deep, steady cultivation. He further entrusted him with another verse: "Suddenly awakening to the fact that there is neither defilement nor purity..."
Movement and stillness are ever in accord; as they alternate, their fragrance continues. I entrust you with the ancestral seal.
The lay practitioner Zhenghan, whose dharma name is Huangqi, is a son of the Ye family from Minxian. By nature he is compassionate and benevolent, and his resolve is upright.
Now over eighty years of age, his spirit remains serene and vigorous; he practices the Way with diligence and vows to bring peace.

While in his final years, he diligently recited the name of Amitābha and sought further instruction from Chan Master Dà'ān. Suddenly, he recalled the essential teachings of the "Single Transmission" (Danyuan).
He addressed the Master, saying, "I am now old; I only hope for a direct pointing. The Master said, "The original nature is birthless; how could there be old age or illness?
The awakened nature is firm and steadfast; one who knows this can bear witness. The wondrous principle of the Single Transmission universally responds to all capacities, fully manifesting itself."
"Essence and function are interpenetrating; through wisdom and concentration, one proceeds directly toward Bodhi. The ultimate aim is the Middle Way.

(Han) Leaped up with joy and bowed, saying, "Having received this profound principle, it deeply accords with my humble heart. Originally there is neither old nor young; how could the Way be east or west?

The Master said, "Since there is neither old nor young, nor east nor west, what kind of principle is this? (Han) Pressed his palms together and recited the Buddha's name. The Master said, "You should take care of yourself."
He further entrusted me with this verse: "Constantly mindful of Amitābha through right practice, Suddenly awakening to the supreme and wondrous subtle mechanism.
Through the auspicious convergence of past conditions, the fragrant lineage shall be continued; I entrust you with this: when the time comes, you shall realize its marvel."
The practitioner Guoti’s dharma name was Dayong. He was the son of Lin of Gaohu in Minnan.
One day the Master saw him and asked, "How do you cultivate your life during your daily activities? He replied, "I constantly recollect the Buddha. The Master said, "Where is the Buddha?
(Guoti) joined his palms at his chest and stood there in silence. The Master said, "What auspicious omen is this? (Guoti) stepped forward.
He first performed a prostration and then spoke this verse: "Formless and traceless, wondrous and boundless, It encompasses the three thousand and the great thousandfold worlds.

Appearing in response to the needs of the occasion—this is the true core; Prajñā ever abides in the sky where night never falls. The Master sealed him with these words, saying, "You are well-suited to the genuine and pure.
He further entrusted him with another verse: "The single branch of spring brought forth on Vulture Peak— I now bestow it upon you as well."
The same. I only entrust you, O worthy one, to treat this with due respect. When the time comes, join the ranks of the illustrious to repay the ancestral tradition.
The monk Guǒ, whose Dharma name is Sāṃkhyeya, is a native of Jiangxi. Carrying incense in his breast, he went to pay his respects, his resolve being to seek the true seal of realization.
The Master struck his teeth three times and asked, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not know. He then requested instruction. The Master—

He said: "The 'True' refers to the Dharmakāya, pure and equal to empty space. The 'Seal' refers to the perfection and subtlety of wisdom and practice, which are harmoniously integrated and unimpeded, to be utilized within this very moment without traversing kalpas of aeons.
This is what you have possessed from the beginning; do not give rise to groundless doubt. (The fruit: Suddenly, he attained a realization and said:
"It was originally complete! There is no need to seek it elsewhere. It is suddenly manifested right where one is—truly inconceivable!"
The Master saw [the meaning] and gave his seal of approval, saying, "So it is, so it is. He further entrusted him with a verse:

"The purport of settling the mind before the crags of Shaoshi, Continuing the flame and linking the fragrance through three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas*. I now entrust this to you; you should hold it dear. The time has come to illuminate the ancestors and manifest wonders after awakening."
The *Sengzheng* (Chief Administrator of the Sangha), Ying, whose posthumous name was Xinghai, was the son of the Dong family from Minnan.

He sought instruction from Chan Master Dagan and received his formal ordination under Chan Master Zhenkong. One day, he requested the Patriarch’s treasury of the true Dharma-eye. The Patriarch said, "Wait until the moon rises over the western mountains, and I shall tell you.
Upon returning, he reported this to his teacher, who said, "The Patriarchs have transmitted the seal of the mind; were it not for wisdom, it could not be continued."
He remained in doubt for one year. One day, his mass of doubt was suddenly shattered. He immediately celebrated this, saying, "This is not the work of another," and presented a verse:
"Originally there is neither above nor below; The perfect light corresponds to empty space. Pervasive and penetrating throughout the Dharma-realm, Tranquil illumination accords with the True Source.

The Patriarch questioned him to verify his realization and granted him approval, saying, "You should cherish yourself. He further entrusted him with a verse on the Mind-Seal of the Buddhas and Patriarchs. To the ultimate Mind-Seal of the Buddhas and Patriarchs...

Now, the wondrous, perfect, pure, and radiant [Dharma] continues the supreme vehicle. Entrust it to worthy talent; it should be held in high esteem. When the conditions and time are ripe, one shall receive the successor.
Sengyuan Tao, whose Dharma name is Dachao, is a son of the Lin family from Min County. He requested further instruction from Chan Master Yuanhai.
The Master had studied under Chan Master Zhenkong. One day, he requested instruction on the method of "the single eye.

The Patriarch said, "Wait until the waters of the South River run dry, and then I shall tell you. Upon returning, the Master conveyed this to his teacher. His teacher remained silent and indicated his understanding.

After a long while, the teacher asked, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not yet grasp this meaning. The teacher said, "When the deluded mind comes to rest, that is Bodhi. He pondered this for one year.
Suddenly, one morning, his doubts were shattered all at once. He immediately said, "To swallow it all in a single gulp is not difficult," and he presented this verse:
"Silent and desolate, it is fundamentally thus; Responding to conditions as they arise, its full manifestation is revealed. The universe is so vast and expansive that it cannot contain it."

Reflecting back and turning the light inward, one enters the courtyard of awakening. When the Patriarch questioned him on this, he immediately realized it within his own mind. "You should cultivate and sustain this yourself," the Patriarch said, and further entrusted him with a verse:
"The Patriarch’s seal of Caoxi stamps the source of the mind; Instantly entering the ocean of Dharma, one stills the wild rush of delusions.
From now on, you must cherish this direct pointing; When the time comes, you must follow the Patriarch’s transmission."
The monk Zhenzhi, whose dharma name was Fawuhuai, was the son of the Chen family from Fuqing County.

He received his formal training under Chan Master Yuanqing and sought further instruction from Chan Master Donghui. He went to visit the Master [Xuedou] and requested an indication of the essential truth of the Great Way.
The Master held up his whisk and, after a long pause, asked, "Do you understand? Zhenzhi replied, "I do not. The Master said, "It is beyond words and speech."

He said: "It is neither self nor person, neither subject nor object; it is neither great nor small, neither pleasant nor painful. It manifests clearly in every head and is fully revealed in every thing.
Ehi! Why do you fail to realize this? You should quickly awaken! At these words, [Zhēnzhì] suddenly attained realization and immediately spoke a verse:

"The essence is fundamentally without obstruction, Universally manifesting throughout the sands of the world-systems. From ancient times until now it has always been thus, Neither diminished nor increased."

[Huai]sui immediately questioned him regarding essence and function, motion and stillness; [the Master’s] profound subtlety was in perfect accord with these. The Master then granted his seal of approval, saying, "You should cultivate yourself.

He further entrusted him with a verse: "The flower blooms at the tip of the pestle, fresh to this very day; To continue the lineage and join the fragrance, you have long possessed the karmic affinity.
Entrust this to worthy talent to uphold and maintain it; The six perfections, the three bodies, and the single nature are all perfected."
Now, this person named Fale (法濂), whose dharma name is Yingqiao, is a son of the Kui clan from Min County. He has observed the precepts for many years and has specialized in the Lotus Sutra.
One day, he requested that his teacher point out to him a great causal connection appearing in the world. The teacher gazed directly at him;
after a long while, he said, "Do you understand? He replied, "I do not comprehend. The teacher said, "Two or three is not the truth; it is only this."

One matter is as it is. (Guo Lian) attained realization upon hearing these words and immediately presented a verse, saying: "Neither going nor coming, ancient and yet present; Originally pure, in harmony with the Heavenly Truth.
Wondrous response and perfect penetration arise from mastery; Majestically and alone, it reveals its radiance.
The Master questioned him closely and granted his approval, entrusting him with a verse: "The spring of a single branch has been transmitted from Vulture Peak; Through past affinities..."

Our karmic affinity has brought us together today; it is a cause for celebration that we may join in the preservation of this noble lineage. When the time comes, you must surely propagate the ancestral wind.
Now, there is one named Zhengmi of Huanggang; he is the son of the Ye family of Min County. Having observed the precepts for many years, his conduct and virtue are refined and pure.
He sought instruction from Chan Master Daaan, and one day requested a teaching on the essential points of the Dharma. The Master struck the desk once.
The Master asked, "Do you understand? He replied, "I am not yet familiar with the Great Meaning. The Master said, "Perfect penetration is free from obstruction;
realize it before what has been heard. (Zhengmi) Suddenly he attained realization and said to himself, "This wondrous time is not obtained from without."

The Master’s seal is thus; you should cultivate it deeply within yourself. He further entrusted them with this verse: "Originally and fundamentally complete, Suddenly awakened as not being something else.
Guard well the ultimate, true, and pure, And the ancestral flame shall continue in fragrant succession."
This Guo Chai, whose dharma name is Mingzhai, is the son of the Ruan family of Min County. He is filial, righteous, benevolent, and wise;
his resolve is sincere and his character is firm and resolute. Having observed the precepts for over ten years, he has attained profound mastery of the Mahāyāna.
One day, the Master saw him and asked, "By a fortunate convergence of past affinities, I venture to ask: where is Mingzhai from? Guo Chai replied, "The body itself is expansive and manifest."
"Amitābha is entirely the true mark (*dharmatā*). The Master asked again, "What is the cause for practicing the Way and observing the fasts?

He replied, "Awakening does not depend on others at all. The Master said, "Constantly outside the gate, you project subject and object. He replied, "Suddenly entering samādhi, one is personally close to the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
He then presented this verse: "The illusory is changed, yet the real is difficult to change; The boat moves, yet the shore does not move. Suchness is without..."
"Extremely wonderful! You have suddenly and thoroughly penetrated the form of the great void. The Master questioned him to confirm his realization, and [the disciple] responded with refined purity.

He was further entrusted with a verse: "Grinding a tile to make a mirror awakens true illumination; Continuing the flame and linking the radiance reaches down to this day. Entrust this to the Eastern Lord; you should hold it in deep respect.
When the time comes, awaken after enlightenment and shine upon the ancestral hall."
Seng Zhengheng, whose style name was Hegang, was the son of the Hu family of Guixi County in Guangzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi.
He sought instruction from Chan Master Baofeng and received his monastic precepts from Chan Master Zhenkong. While his teacher was instructing the assembly, he heard the *Lotus Sūtra* state:
"The Buddhas appear in the world for one great matter. (Heng) remained deluded and did not awaken; furthermore, he heard the Great...
Chao asked for the method to attain "one eye. The Patriarch said, "I shall tell you when the waters of the Southern River have run dry.

(Heng) His doubts and deliberations increased further, leaving him restless in both sleep and food. Suddenly, he attained sudden enlightenment and said to himself: "The river of consciousness has dried up; there is only the profound stillness of true reality.
The four currents turn back, and the waves of the hundred rivers subside. He went straight to the Patriarch’s quarters and presented this verse: "The pure body is suchness (*tathatā*)."
Spontaneously unrolling or rolling up as it may, originally there is not a single thing. In a blink of an eye, the entire body is revealed.

When the Patriarch inquires and tests for certification, one must undergo deep refinement. He further entrusts this with a verse: "The mind-seal of the direct pointing, transmitted alone, From now on, nurture it until it reaches the utmost purity.
Concentration and wisdom should be balanced, without partiality; When the time comes, you must propagate the Patriarch's wind."
The one here named Yuan Cheng, whose dharma name is Yingkong, is the son of the Zheng family of Fengshan in Min County.

Having observed the precepts for many years, he is filial, benevolent, and compassionate. He has studied the Mahayana with great diligence and is determined to seek the Great Way, having requested instruction from Chan Master Zhenkong.
He requested instruction on a single great causal condition (*mahānidāna*). The Master pointed directly at him. He asked, "Is this one? Is this great?

Suddenly, [Hui]teng attained realization and said, "It has been fundamentally and originally complete; it is neither lacking nor superfluous. He immediately entered *samādhi*, and his radiance filled the vast void.

The Master certified him, saying, "You should skillfully sustain this. Furthermore, I entrust you with this verse: 'The True Dharma seals the mind-source; it is the direct pointing transmission outside the teachings.'"
Fortunately, he encountered the succession of the "Flowering Fragrance" lineage, preserving the ultimate truth and purity.

The monk Yuan was given the Dharma name Tongquan; he was the son of the Liu family from Hougan County. He received his training under Chan Master Zhenkong and relied upon the cultivation of precepts, concentration, and wisdom.
Broadening his compassionate wisdom and his vows of practice, one day he contemplated the essentials of the Dharma and sought his teacher.
The Master revealed [the truth]. He bowed his head and asked, "Do you see? The disciple replied, "I see. The Master said, "The nature of seeing is distinct;

it is neither form nor sound, and it is not obtained from without. One who awakens can realize it. At these words, the disciple suddenly attained realization and said, "The Way is fundamentally formless, spanning from antiquity to the present.

To behold its face is to have nothing hidden. It is my good fortune to have met one who understands. The Master gave his seal of approval, saying, "You should cultivate this deeply until it reaches a state of true purity."
Purity. He further entrusted him with a verse: "A single shout like a thunderclap; the succession of the fragrant blossoms reaches Yuan Ying. His heroic spirit deserves respect;
the time has come to illuminate the ancestral temple."
Sengyuan’s dharma name was Huiquan. He was the son of the Zhuo family from Houguan County. He received his training under Chan Master Zhikong.

One day, he entered the master’s room and requested the essentials of the Dharma. The Master gave a shout and asked, "What essential Dharma is this? Sengyuan, failing to grasp it, again sought the Ultimate Way.
The Master raised an eyebrow to indicate it and asked, "Do you understand? Sengyuan replied, "I do not. The Master said, "It is not."
That which was previously sought externally is now realized as being inherently possessed within oneself. Suddenly awakening to this, he spoke a verse: "Quiescent and still, the fundamental suchness;

How could its wondrous function be constrained? Perfectly full is true compassion; Mysterious and profound, its glory is more than sufficient. The Patriarch examined him with questions and granted his seal of approval, saying:
"You should deeply cultivate the true and pure. He further entrusted him with another verse: "The great meaning of the West is mind-sealing the mind; From lamp to lamp, the flame continues to burn."
Now, from this point forward, the finger-pointing has been thoroughly clarified; when the time comes, one must succeed to the ancestral hall.
This person, whose name is Guohui and whose style name is Daqian, is the son of the Chen family of Huai’an County.

Having observed the precepts and recited the Buddha’s name, he investigated the ultimate truth until he suddenly attained realization, whereupon he presented this verse: "When one dharma is penetrated, all dharmas are penetrated. Receiving this...

The Gate of Non-duality is revealed through instruction; responding to the capacity of the occasion, manifestation is without partiality. By reflecting inwardly and returning the light, one merges with the original source.

When the Master examines and interrogates you for certification, you should cultivate yourself within. He further entrusted this verse: "The Inexhaustible Lamp spreads throughout the great chiliocosm;

Quiescence and clarity are eternally luminous, a sky that never knows night. I now entrust this to you: realize it through the Mind alone. When the time comes, you must receive the worthy successors."
The Vinaya Master Zhengzhi took the dharma name Xiaotian. He was the son of the Shi family from Jinjiang County in Quanzhou Prefecture.

He received his training under Chan Master Tianjian. One day, the Patriarch saw him and asked, "Zhengzhi, what are you doing? He replied, "In the midst of time, there is no contradiction. The Patriarch said, "If that is so, then let us meet.

He replied, "Right where I am, the majestic presence manifests. Thereupon, he spoke this verse: At the very place where I stand, the majestic form appears; Within the present moment, there is no deviation. If you wish to see me, look right here; The Buddha-nature is vast and boundless.

He said: "Profound stillness and empty spirit persist from antiquity to the present. Majestically manifest, it is most clearly evident. Pure, complete, and transcending the characteristics of space—the great earth, mountains, and rivers are themselves the Buddha-mind.
The Patriarch examined him with questions and granted his seal of approval. He then instructed him to undergo deep refinement and further entrusted him with this verse:
"The robe and Dharma of Huangmei were directly transmitted to the South; The Patriarchal Seal has been inherited through the Gate of Non-duality. I entrust this to you, O man of exceptional talent."
One should honor and uphold [this]. When the time arrives, you shall illuminate your ancestors and continue the succession of fragrant renown.
Now, one named Zheng Zui, whose courtesy name is Yuanquan, is a son of the Lin clan of Min County.

He sought further instruction from Chan Master Dajian, whereupon he received and maintained the precepts and applied himself with diligence to the Way. One day, he entered the inner quarters to request the Great Way; the Master remained silent.
After a long silence, he asked, "Do you understand? The monk replied, "I have not yet awakened. The Master said, "The Great is all-pervasive throughout the universe;
the Way extends everywhere across the Dharma-realm. This is what you inherently possess—neither two nor distinct. If you realize this principle, it is not obtained from without.
At these words, [Zhaozhou] suddenly attained a realization and immediately spoke a verse: "When the occasion arises, it is revealed alone, without concealment. The Great Way has no..."

The partiality of essence and function is fully perfected; its radiant clarity penetrates throughout the sands of the world-realms. Originally pure, it exists eternally. The Master then questioned and examined him for certification, saying:
"You must cultivate yourself deeply, refining away all that is not true or pure. He then bestowed a verse of entrustment: "The single flower of Shaolin has five petals linked;
The udumbara blooms luxuriantly throughout the great thousandfold world. I now show this to you; you should hold it in deep respect. When the time comes, it must..."
He was to succeed the later worthy.
Sengming Gui, whose style name was Honghui, was the son of the Zheng family of Fengshan in Minnan.
He received his training under Chan Master Dachao and sought further instruction from Chan Master Dazhi. One day, he entered the chamber of Chan Master Zhongkong to pay his respects and requested—
He sought the essential meaning of the Dharma. The Patriarch pointed to a lotus flower to show him. When the flower opened, he saw the Buddha and said, "I have shown you the Way.

(Gui) did not yet grasp this principle. He brought forward Master Shangzhi; the Master recited the name of the Buddha once, yet [Gui] still did not understand. He prayed, "I pray that the Master will grant me instruction. The Master said:

Upon touching objects, true *prajñā* suddenly manifested; yet he had not yet attained realization. After more than a year of doubt and deliberation, he suddenly attained an awakening and presented this verse:
"Originally it is a pure thing; how could it be constrained by emerging from the mud? It is in the water but does not enter the water."
"When the flowers bloom, one sees the Buddha. The Patriarch asked, "What is purity? (Gui) folded his hands at his chest and remained silent for a long while.
The Patriarch said, "How is it that you see the Buddha? (Gui) stepped forward and prostrated himself. The Patriarch said, "So it is, so it is."

Support yourself well; you should succeed to the Great Wisdom. He then entrusted him with a verse: "The fundamental pulse has no coming or going; its responsive resonance pervades the sands of the world-realms.
I now entrust it to you to guard; when the time comes, receive the future talent."

Now, Guojun’s Dharma name is Dayun. He is the son of the Hong family of the Three Mountains. Having observed the precepts and practiced with diligent cultivation, he researched the Supreme Vehicle (Mahāyāna).
Suddenly, he attained a realization and presented this verse: "Pointing to Amitābha, I awaken to my original nature; Neither sound nor form, it manifests within the numinous mind.
Profoundly still and tranquil, it penetrates past and present; Its essence and function are perfectly integrated, utterly free from a speck of dust. The Master [said:]...

He granted his seal of approval and exhorted him with profound depth: "It should be pure, immaculate, and wondrous. He further entrusted him with a verse: "Principle and phenomena both manifest within the non-abiding mind;
The perfect capacity universally responds throughout lands as numerous as motes of dust. Originally pure and undefiled, this is the time to continue the flame And illuminate the ancestral temple."

This Guodi, whose style name is Cheng’an, is the son of the Gao family of Min County. Having observed the precepts for many years, one day he reflected: "The World-Honored One held up a flower; Bodhidharma settled the mind.
From patriarch to patriarch, it was transmitted from mind to mind through the seal of the mind.

Yet my own mind has not yet attained realization—how can there be a seal? To reach old age in vain birth, I have been deluded in mind and lost my nature. Thereupon, with earnest resolve, he respectfully entered [the path].
He entered the Master’s quarters and prostrated before the seat. The Master saw him and asked, "What have you been doing all day?
He replied, "I have constantly recited the name of Amitābha. The Master said, "Where is he right now? He replied, "With palms joined, laughing 'he-he'.

The Master said, "Truly, he illuminates the Dharma-realm; you should turn your light inward and enter the three mysteries. He replied, "Only through the compassionate grace of the fundamental teaching have I finally awakened to this vision."

Realizing the One Vehicle by nature, he spoke in verse: "The body of suchness is unmoving and tranquil; True nature is pervasive and transcends words and letters. The true reality of Amitābha is about to appear;
Compassion and wisdom are perfectly luminous throughout the great thousandfold world. The Master asked: "What is it like when it appears?
(Guo Zhi) replied: "One recitation of the Buddha's name. The Master said: "What is this true Amitābha? (Guo Di) stepped forward.

[The student] joined his palms before [the Master]. After remaining silent for a long while, the Master said, "The Seal is as it was. Guard it well yourself; nurture the true and pure. (And so forth. He further entrusted him with a verse:
"The Dharma-seal of Caoxi has been transmitted through ancient and modern times; Through past affinities, you have joyfully encountered it to continue the succession of fragrance.
Entrusted to one who understands, it should be cherished and guarded; Nurture the true and pure, and both essence and function will be complete."
This person, whose name is Guozhu and whose style name is Zhikai, is the son of the Jiang family of Jianyang County.
Having observed the precepts for many years, he has practiced the recitation of the Buddha’s name and Zen meditation, aspiring to attain rebirth in the Land of Peaceful Nurturing (*An-yang*).

Upon hearing that the Master directly points to the nature and clarifies the mind, and that unless one does so, it is not ultimate, he has since carried incense in his breast and respectfully entered the Master’s chamber. Prostrating before the seat, the Master asked: "Who are you?"
[The Master] asked, "Where does the person dwell? He replied, "When one beholds the face, the entire body is manifest. [The Master] asked, "What Dharma do you preach during that time?

He replied, "Amitābha is unstained by dust. He then spoke this verse: "Contemplate the Buddha to investigate the mind; Only then will you realize it is your own true self. I personally offer this mani jewel."
"Pure and naturally luminous. The Master said, "Where is the *maṇi* jewel now? (Gwae-su) recited the Buddha’s name once. The Master said, "I do not ask about the dust; what of Amitābha?
(Gwae-su) stepped forward, joined his palms, and remained silent for a long while. The Master certified him, saying, "It is so.
You must maintain this well. It is truly ultimate, truly pure. He further entrusted him with a verse: "At the Dharma assembly on Vulture Peak, I offered the *maṇi*..."

The Bhikṣuṇī attained sudden enlightenment and realized the perfect clarity of Bodhi. She continued the fragrant lamp of the Patriarchs' Way, ensuring its flame remained unextinguished. Her cultivation of the true and pure was extraordinary after her awakening.
Now, the one named Guohao, whose style name is Yupuo, is the son of the Gao family of Min County; he has observed the precepts for many years. One day—

Reflecting thus, the Sixth Patriarch universally expounded and revealed the Mahāprajñāpāramitā, harmonizing it with the ultimate truth. This Dharma seal was transmitted in succession, a direct pointing through single-lineage transmission.
Thereupon, [the disciple] specially gave rise to sincere devotion, personally entered the Master’s chamber, knelt before his seat, and requested instruction. The Master said:
"Who are you? He replied, "I am Guohao. The Master said, "Guohao pervades the Dharma-realm; you should return to the source and enter samādhi.
He replied, "The fundamental nature reveals the wondrous mystery; upon suddenly attaining true awakening, there is no birth. He then spoke a verse:
"Receiving the Master’s instruction on Amitābha, Sudden enlightenment occurred in a single kṣaṇa. The original true awakening is wondrous; The light of the face [shines upon] the *sattvas*."
"Baha. The Master said, "Where is Amitābha right now? (Guo Hao) stepped forward one pace and held [the robe] up with both hands.
The Master said, "What is it like when you turn the light back upon yourself? (Guo Hao) folded his hands at his chest and remained silent for a long while.

The Master then gave him his seal of approval, saying, "Guard and maintain this well; nurture its true purity," and so forth. He further instructed him with a verse: The robe and Dharma of Huangmei...
Entrusted to Naneng: Having awakened to and entered the Perfect School, he continues the succession of the fragrant lineage. Entrust this to those of like mind; they should treat it with reverence.
Cultivating true purity, he shall illuminate the ancestral hall.
Now, Guoen has received the title Dahei. He is the second son of Li Ganbing of the Three Mountains, who has observed the fasts and precepts for many years with devotion.
He sincerely requested instruction. He entered the master’s quarters in person and prostrated before the seat. When the master saw him, he asked, "Who are you?
He replied, "I am a son of the Buddha, observing the fast. The master said, "Where is the Buddha now? He replied, "His majestic light penetrates the great void.
The master spoke a verse: "The ancient Way is truly level and plain; Pure and serene, it is free from even the finest speck of dust. Coming and going, one acts with sovereign ease."
The Master said, "One who has attained awakening sees true illumination. (Guo En) [asked], "What is this majestic radiance? He shouted toward the blue sky.
The Master said, "How is it that this is true illumination? (Guo En) stepped forward to pay his respects and then returned to his original position.

The Master said, "If it is so, you should skillfully support and nurture it until it is pure and refined," and so forth. He further entrusted him with a verse: "The wooden ball on the snowy peaks remains to this day; it is round."
The vital spirit is lively, continuing the succession of the fragrant flowers. With brilliant insight, one suddenly awakens to inherit this intent. I entrust you:
at all times, you must emulate the ancestral transmission. Now, the one formally named Qingquan is the son of the Lin family of Fucheng County.

Having observed the fast for many years, one day he heard from his dharma friends that he had obtained the authentic prediction of the Xuanshi lineage, which directly points to the mind and reveals the nature—the great matter of cause and effect.
The conditions were such that, with unceasing shame and remorse, he attained sudden penetration. "Why have I been so obstructed? If I do not awaken now, my future regrets will be in vain.
With resolute sincerity, he went in person to the Patriarch’s chamber and prostrated himself before the seat. Seeing him, the Patriarch asked, "From where have you come?
He replied, "I beg for your compassion to transmit the True Dharma. The Patriarch said, "If it is shown directly, how could it be hidden? He replied:
He first realized that [the mind] arises from the mind. The Patriarch said, "Now that you know it arises from the mind, you should turn the light back upon yourself and enter *samādhi*.
He replied, "By virtue of encountering and receiving your wondrous instructions, I shall return to the source right where I am and realize the One Vehicle.

He then spoke this verse: "Pure and clear, fundamentally empty and numinous; Suchness, wondrous, perfect, and luminous. Pervading and penetrating worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, This True Person alone is revealed. The Patriarch said, "Wondrous!"
"What is your intention? (Zheng Qin) bowed his head three times. The Patriarch asked, "How do you act to return to the source?

(Zheng Qin) joined his palms and remained silent, then returned to his original position. The Patriarch confirmed it was so, saying, "You must maintain this well and guard it until you reach the state of true purity.

He further entrusted him with a verse: "The plucking of the flower to show the assembly—a small measure of understanding; Kāśyapa’s subtle smile—the secret transmission continues. Through past affinities..."
He divided the continuity of the lamp’s flame and entrusted you with the task of illuminating the ancestral temple when the time comes.
His monastic name is Zhenzhi, and his dharma name is Wuhuai. He was the son of the Chen family from Min County.

He received formal instruction from Chan Master Yuanqing and sought further guidance from Chan Master Donghui. At that time, he came before me and requested an indication of the essential truth of the Great Way. The Master raised [his finger].
He raised his fly-whisk and showed it to him, asking, "Do you understand? The student replied, "I do not. The Master said, "It is apart from words and language;

it is not something produced by self or others. For what reason do you fail to awaken? You have heard it with your ears and seen it with your eyes. (Zhi) suddenly attained realization and immediately spoke this verse:

The essence is fundamentally without obstruction; it manifests universally throughout the sands of worlds. It has always been thus from antiquity to the present; it neither diminishes nor decays. The Master questioned him further:

"When essence and function are in perfect accord, you should refine yourself deeply until you reach the state of pure subtlety. He then offered this verse as an entrustment: "The flower blooms upon the pestle’s tip, fresh even to this day.
To continue this succession of fragrant blossoms, one must have a karmic affinity. I entrust this to you, O worthy talent; you should hold it in deep reverence."
Of great magnanimity and brilliant intelligence, his singular nature was perfected.
His dharma name was Guoyuan Qingtang; he was the son of the Yang family from Min Province. Through fasting and precepts, he cultivated his vows, desiring to succeed to the True Vehicle.
He investigated the profound and subtle, mastering the wondrous principles. One day, he suddenly attained realization and immediately presented this verse: "The Original..."
Coming, there is no lack; throughout the ten directions, it manifests clearly. At all times, without interruption, its essence and function are constantly seen by oneself.
The Master examined the subtle truth; it accorded perfectly and was not external. You should refine yourself through elimination and nurture this state until it is pure.
He further entrusted me with a verse: *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā*: Suddenly awakening that the source is originally not to be sought outside, I entrust you to the moment of perfect clarity.
The majestic spiritual power illuminates the great trichiliocosm.

Now, the one whose formal dharma name is Zhengshu Jùnquán was the daughter of the Ruan family of Min County. Devoted to filial piety and compassion, she observed the precepts and attained wisdom through the Buddha-vehicle.
She sought instruction from Chan Master Dà'ān and, in her quest for the profound mystery, constantly attended at the ancestral temple. One day, suddenly—

There was a point of realization; he then presented this verse: "The treasury of treasures within the essence is self-governed; Opened wide, it shines brightly, its wondrous perfection fully manifest.

Let go of even a single hair’s breadth, and from the start nothing is established; The pure land is harmoniously integrated, pervading the ten directions. The Master examined his subtle truth and found it accorded with the ultimate principle.
He instructed him: "You should nurture this deeply until you reach perfect clarity. He further entrusted him with another verse: "High Peak reveals the True Lineage."

A person of great capacity, beholding my face and accepting the responsibility with inconceivable realization. I entrust you to always preserve and maintain this; when the time comes, you must continue this marvelous legacy.
This individual, whose dharma name is Guoyuan and whose style name is Jing’an, is the son of the Lin family of Min County. He has observed the precepts and fasts for many years.

While practicing the mindfulness of the Buddha without interruption, amidst a state of tranquil concentration, he suddenly beheld a sublime vision. Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva appeared to instruct him in the practice of mindfulness of the Buddha.

With his mind and speech in perfect accord, he went specifically to the Master’s chamber to seek the Teacher’s guidance toward the ultimate Way. The Master said: "The wondrous principle of the ultimate Way..."
Free from all vain expectations, [one realizes that] dreams and illusions are unreal and not ultimate.

Rather, by turning the light back upon itself, one suddenly awakens to the true and eternal, which is perfectly luminous and complete, fundamentally equal, and not obtained from without. (Yuan) Suddenly realizing this, he spoke a verse, saying:

"The fundamental essence is originally pure; Its radiance pervades the great thousandfold world. True and eternal, it neither increases nor decreases; Its wondrous function universally encompasses all. The Master—

He questioned him thoroughly and granted his seal of approval, saying: "You should be excellent, true, and pure. He further entrusted him with a verse: "The Patriarch came to directly point the way, transmitting outside the teachings;

Flowers joined in fragrance, succeeding one another down to Guo Yuan. I entrust you, worthy gentleman, that you should preserve this; Cultivate it with true purity, so that essence and function are complete."
This Guohuai, whose Dharma name is Taquan, is the son of the Xiao family of the Three Mountains. By nature he is benevolent and compassionate, and in his heart he maintains rectitude.
Having observed the precepts for many years, his aspirations have been directed toward Bodhi. One day the Master saw him and asked, "What is your name?
He replied, "Taquan. The Master said, "Taquan penetrates the Dharma-realm; throughout the ten directions, it is the perfect, singular, true luminosity."
The Master said: "Originally, when the Buddha was on Vulture Peak, if one dharma is thoroughly understood, all dharmas are thoroughly understood.
Hui-guai said: "What is this 'one dharma'? [He] loudly recited the name of the Buddha. The Master said: "Where is Vulture Peak right now? [He] placed his palms together at his chest.
After remaining silent for a long while, the Master spoke a verse, saying: "The various marks are no-marks, unstained by dust; Pervading the entire realm of sands, it is the single true luminosity.
In every step of entering and exiting, there is nothing other than this; It fills all of space—the body of the ancient Buddha. The Master said, "It is so."
"You should refine yourself deeply until you reach the state of true purity. He further entrusted him with this verse: "A single branch from Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa has been transmitted afar;
It is like an utpala flower blooming amidst the flames. I now entrust it to you; you must cherish it well. When wisdom and practice are integrated, one reaches the highest terrace."
The monk Renhuai, whose Dharma name was Yangshi, was the son of the Wen family from Fucing County. He received his formal training under the Ācārya Shaoshi.
One day, reflecting upon the essential principles of the Chan school, he brought incense and entered the master’s room to request direct instruction on the Great Way.
The Master said: "Direct pointing is indeed not absent; how could the Great Way be obstructed? If the clouds of delusion suddenly part, clarity will be seen right where one stands.
(Huai) Suddenly attained realization and spoke this verse: "Originally it was not another thing; Not having awakened, I merely constrained myself.
Suddenly realizing the power of the bestowed grace, It is clear and free from all restriction. The Master certified him, saying: "It is as you have realized. You should maintain this well. To—[End]
"Pure and wondrous—this all stems from you. I further entrust you with this verse: 'The essence and function of the single staff are revealed; the ultimate Way transcends words and phrases.
May you respectfully continue [the lineage]; when the time comes, you shall find those with whom you have affinity.'"
