This person, whose Dharma name is Zhengming Daxian, is the son of the Su family of Pingjiang.
He practiced medicine to compassionately aid the multitude, observed the precepts with diligent cultivation, and aspired to Bodhi, desiring its swift realization.

He requested instruction from Chan Master Da’an and reverently sought his guidance, asking: "By what method may one cultivate so as to reach Bodhi swiftly? The Master replied: "Dharmas are fundamentally non-existent."
Awakening is not swift. When seeing forms or hearing sounds, they naturally revert; there is neither long nor short, neither red nor green—pure, translucent, and clear.
This is one's original face. (Ming) Suddenly realizing this, he spoke a verse: "Vast and expansive, it encompasses the Dharma-realm."
Fully manifesting throughout the ten directions, the inherently pure essence appears as auspicious light everywhere. The Patriarch questioned him to grant his seal of approval;

you should now deeply cultivate your true and pure nature. He further entrusted him with a verse: "The Dharma intent from the West is the mind-sealing of mind; The flame continues and the fragrance links to the Zhengming era.
Having met through past karmic conditions, you should treat this with reverence; The time has come to glorify the Patriarchs and awaken those who follow."
The Dharma name of this person, Guozhao, is Jiang. He is the son of the Wang family of Shuangjing Village in Jianyang County.

Having observed the precepts for many years, he has cultivated various meritorious practices. His teacher instructed him to practice *nianfo* (Buddha-recitation), so that merit and wisdom might be cultivated together. Pressing his mind in deep inquiry, he asks:
"Who is it? Do not dwell in emptiness or existence; do not distinguish between east and west. You must simply seek clarity regarding the fundamental style of your own house. Please accept this.
"Herein lies my instruction: remain at every thought-moment without departing from it. (Zhao) suddenly attained realization and spoke this verse:
"Reciting the Buddha’s name, I awaken to true nature; It does not depart from the original mind. At all times, it is ever unobscured, Pervading and uniting with the City of Ultimate Bliss.

The Master said, "When it is unobscured, what is it like? (Zhao) stepped forward to pay his respects. The Master said, "Right now, you must clearly discern the nature of your mind. (Zhao) joined his palms.
Recite the Buddha’s name and return to your original place. The Master said, "It is so. Guard and maintain this well for yourself until it reaches the state of pure refinement.
He further entrusted him with a verse: "Cultivate both merit and wisdom without falling into partiality; Advancing toward Bodhi, you shall succeed the Patriarchs.
I only entrust you to support this well—cherish it with care; When the land is adorned, the seven-jeweled lotus shall bloom."

This person, Guowen, whose dharma name is Shaoren, is the son of the Yang family of the Three Mountains. By nature he is benevolent and compassionate; in conduct he establishes himself in filial piety and righteousness.
He has observed the precepts for many years, possessing profound faith, understanding, and diligence. His male and female relatives at home share his aspiration for pure cultivation.

Having researched the True Vehicle and attained a clear realization of the wondrous Way, one day he contemplated the direct pointing to the orthodox lineage. With reverent sincerity, he entered the master’s chamber. The Master—
Seeing him looking back, [the Master] raised his voice and asked, "Who is it? He replied, "It is Guowen. The Master said, "Guowen transcends the ocean of Dharma;

through wondrous perfection and purity, he realizes Bodhi. [Guowen] replied, "Prajñā accords with the great chiliocosm; when practice and vows are both manifested, one attains Perfect Enlightenment. He then presented this verse:
"Originally pure, radiating brilliant light, The provisional and the real are both manifested, penetrating antiquity."
"Now, the profound principle of the three emptinesses is the true wondrous function; throughout the great chiliocosm of sand-grain worlds, his entire body is manifested.

The Master said, "By the convergence of past conditions, we have fortunately met. May I ask, Venerable One, where are you from? (The monk) stepped forward and replied, "Having planted causes over many kalpas, how could the Compassionate Honored One fail to seek out his inferior son?
The Master said, "I do not ask about 'compassion' or 'inferior'; who is this 'honored son'? (The monk) joined his palms and recited:
The Buddha said: "The Seal of the Master is thus. You should support it well until you reach the state of true purity, perfect illumination, and sovereign freedom.

He further entrusted them with this verse: "The Blue Ancestor’s direct pointing allows the mind to rest; The flame continues and the fragrance links to Shao Ren. Entrust this to worthy talents who shall preserve it;
When conditions meet, repay the debt of gratitude by receiving future generations."
This man, whose dharma name is Zhengzhi (Zhengzhi), is a son of the Lin family from Min County. By nature he is compassionate and benevolent, and in his resolve he is tranquil and detached.
Having lost both parents at an early age, he set his mind upon transcending the world of toil and suffering. He received instruction from Chan Master Tiandong.
One day, the Master saw him and asked, "What is the reason for your constant earnestness? Zhengzhi replied, "Day and night, I am devoted to recitation and advancement."
Gongti, the Patriarch said, "Be unrestrained; do not be attached to 'others' or 'me'. Gongti replied, "I have suddenly cast off this scripture and tucked it away.
He then presented a verse, saying: "Originally there is no obstruction; Pure and clear, always autonomous. The Honored One of Suchness, immovable, Suddenly transcends all things beyond.
The Patriarch asked, "What does it mean to transcend all things beyond? Gongti clapped his hands and recited the Buddha’s name. The Patriarch said, "Purity!"

"How is it? (Zhizhu) pressed his palms together at his chest. The Patriarch immediately granted him approval. "You must refine yourself deeply until you reach absolute purity. He further entrusted him with a verse:
"The flower blooms on Mount Shaoshi and its fragrance remains to this day; Its continuity flows on, extending from Dragon Spring. Entrust this to those of like mind; they should honor and uphold it.
In these times, let compassion and wisdom take effect as the Patriarch’s legacy."
On this occasion, Zhengtan Faxiao Xianglin was a son of the Zhang family from Min County. By nature he was gentle and mild; he was compassionate, filial, and righteous.
He cultivated the precepts of fasting with diligence and aspired to the loftiness of the noble sages. Abruptly renouncing his domestic ties, he left the mundane world to study the Way.

He received instruction from Chan Master Tianjian, serving the monastic affairs with earnest devotion, attending to his teacher with respectful compliance, and treating the assembly with humility and harmony. One day...
Reflecting upon the unsurpassed, wondrous Way, he manifested exceptional sincerity and respectfully proceeded to the Patriarch’s chamber.

Bowing his head before the seat, the Patriarch saw him and asked, "Are you capable of serving as a ridgepole or a beam? (Tán) replied, "I shall surely uphold the ancient model. The Patriarch said, "Right now, brandish an axe.
He replied, "Directly beneath it, *svāhā*. He then spoke this verse: "A single ray of numinous light pervades the great void."
Illuminating the ten directions without exception, the wondrousness within this present clapping of hands is manifest. The ancient moon and the clear spring correspond to the fundamental suchness.
The Patriarch asked, "What is this wondrousness? Zhengtan stepped forward, offered incense, and said, "Respectfully, we offer this universal offering.
The Patriarch asked, "What is this correspondence with fundamental suchness? (Tan) performed his inquiry and returned to his original position. The Patriarch immediately granted him approval.
You should cultivate yourself deeply and refine yourself until you are pure. Subsequently, under the Heavenly Mirror, he further entrusted him with a verse:
"The mind-seal of the Buddhas and Patriarchs continues to this very day; Lamp after lamp, the flame is transmitted in succession. I rejoice that your past affinities possess their share;
May you sustain the final age and spread the Restoration."

The one now formally receiving the Dharma name Haquan (White Spring) is a son of the Zheng clan from Fucheng County. By nature he is compassionate and benevolent; in his resolve, he is devoted to filial conduct.
He has refined himself through the observance of *upavāsa* and precepts, with a mind intent on transcending the dust and toil of worldly existence.

Having received instruction from Chan Master Tiandong, he has mastered the principles of the teachings and investigated their profound subtleties. One day, the Patriarch saw him and asked: "Regarding the affairs of daily life, what is it like?"

"What? Hu asked. Zuzhi replied, "Your service to the master and attendance upon the assembly have resulted in too much leakage. Hu said, "I shall cease following after sounds and forms to wander outside.

Zuzhi said, "If you suddenly awaken and turn the light back within to enter *samādhi*, then present me with a verse. Hu immediately presented this verse: "The original state is wondrous, void, and spiritual;

Pure and still, it is naturally perfect and luminous. Everywhere there is no greed or defilement; It is utterly detached from the dust of the six sense organs. Zuzhi said, "You must always remain thus."

"You should carefully preserve and maintain this, nurturing it with purity. You may succeed to Tian Tong. Furthermore, I entrust you with this verse: The source of Caoxi flows on and is transmitted to this day;
Dense and continuous, reaching down to the heroic spirit. I entrust you to always preserve and guard it; The time has come to continue the flame and illuminate the ancestral hall."
This person, whose Dharma name is now being formally conferred as Qichuan, is the son of the Xia family of Fucheng County. By nature he is benevolent and wise;

in his resolve, he acts with impartiality. From childhood he abhorred meat and pungent flavors, and as he grew older, he took pleasure in literary composition. Because his parents passed away early, he felt unable to repay their kindness through worldly means.

Thus, he purified his mind and observed the precepts, offering his sincere devotion to the holy and the true, vowing that his parents might transcend to a higher realm, and renouncing fame and office to pursue the Way.

Dao left the secular world to enter the monastic order at Shuanglong, where he received his training under Chan Master Tiandong. His master commanded him to record the entirety of the teachings and lineages of Miaokong.
One day, he reflected that from the sages of antiquity to the worthies of later times, all had sacrificed their bodies for the sake of the Dharma;

like one lamp kindling another, their brilliance has shone through the ages from past to present. "What person am I? he thought. "If I do not humble my own spirit now, I shall merely labor in vain for those who come after."
He repented and entered the room with utmost sincerity. When the Patriarch saw him, he asked, "What is your name? He replied, "Zhengdi. The Patriarch said, "Zhengdi emits radiance;
you should cultivate and conceal it to await the time for its use. (Zhengdi) replied, "Prajñā is fundamentally numinous and penetrating."
From this true inquiry, it manifested instantaneously. He immediately presented a verse, saying: "The essence is fundamentally unborn, empty and silent;

Perfectly luminous, universally responding, its wondrousness is infinite. Clearly and suddenly detached from the realms of sense-faculties and objects, It is free and spontaneously fused—this is the bliss of the holy truth.
The Patriarch asked, "What is 'universally responding'? [Zheng Ding] cried out at the top of his voice, "Master! The Patriarch asked, "What is the state of being 'free and spontaneous'?"

(Chengji) joined his palms at his chest and remained silent for a long while. The Patriarch immediately granted him approval, saying: "You should maintain this well until you reach the state of true purity;
you shall succeed to Tian-dong. He further entrusted him with a verse: "The Linji school’s style is loftier than the extraordinary;
Flowers of fragrance connect, spreading blessings through heroic heirs. I entrust you with earnest sincerity—treasure it well! In these times, after awakening, sing the Patriarch’s song."
This person, Zheng Tang, courtesy name Jingquan, is a son of the Zhang family from Fucheng County. By nature he is gentle and kind; in his resolve he is upright and honest.

He reveres benevolence and practices righteousness, being loyal, trustworthy, and diligent in his efforts. Having lost both parents at an early age, he single-mindedly aspired to the Way, renouncing the secular world to enter the monastic life.
He sought out sages and visited friends, receiving instruction from Chan Master Tiandong and serving under the monk Xingde.
Shou spent day and night in diligent toil, realizing that self and others are non-dual. One day he saw the assembly striving together to reach the ultimate goal;

desiring to seek Bodhi, he took the clarification of the mind as the foundation. He thought with self-reproach, "Everyone here possesses the will to penetrate the profound and subtle mysteries, yet why is my wisdom so slow?
Even now I remain unenlightened. Thereupon, with a resolute heart, he respectfully entered the Patriarch’s chamber and prostrated before him, entreating only for his instruction.
Zhaozhou showed [the lad] to the Patriarch, who asked, "How is your daily activity? The lad replied, "I am gathering firewood to serve as the steward.

The Patriarch said, "Reflect carefully: by whose power is this done? The lad replied, "Whatever goes against my will is entirely me. He then spoke a verse: "Originally there are no forms or traces; It encompasses and pervades the great thousandfold world.
Everywhere there is no obstruction; It constantly radiates white light. The Patriarch asked, "How is it that there is no obstruction?"
(Zhengtang) loudly recited the Buddha’s name. The Patriarch said, "What can the great trichiliocosm possibly contain? (Zhengtang) remained silent for a long while.

The Patriarch confirmed this, saying, "Having been refined and polished until you shine, you are fit to succeed Tian-dong. He further entrusted him with a verse: "Planting pines and carrying grain is the ancestral style;
The seal of the true dharma and its principle are the same. Through past affinities, you have met this auspicious assembly to inherit this teaching; I entrust it to you at this time."
Shaozu Long. Herein is Zhengxie, styled Zhenquan; he is the son of Lin of the Three Mountains. By nature benevolent and compassionate, he has planted the roots of virtue in past lives.
From youth his resolve was for pure cultivation, and as he grew, he drew near to the worthy and good. Reflecting on the boundless kindness of his parents and mindful of the fleeting nature of time...

Swiftly he cleansed his heart and purified his thoughts, observing the precepts with sincere devotion. He prayed that his parents might obtain merit and goodness, and established the resolve to study for Bodhi.

Under the tutelage of Master Tiansi, he practiced the Dharma according to the essential mysteries of the Mahāyāna. One day, while visiting the patriarchal quarters, he beheld the "dragons and elephants" at the Dharma assembly;
their words transcended all conventions and every phrase accorded with the school’s tenets, thereby continuing the fragrant lineage of the ancestral path.
He sought to perpetuate the lineage of the Buddhas. (Zheng Xie) Feeling an inexhaustible sense of shame, he thought, "He is a great master;

what person am I? Having failed to reach him, I have spent my years in vain. Thereupon, with sincere devotion, he prostrated himself before the Master’s seat. The Patriarch asked him, "For what reason have you left the household life?
He replied, "To escape the dust of the world, I seek to realize the mind. The Patriarch asked, "Where is your mind? He replied, "I see it..."
Upon hearing this, Wenjiangdangren immediately presented a verse, saying: "Originally there is no dust or obstruction; Purity arises from mastery. Prajñā is ever manifest before one;
Its radiance pervades the sands of the world. The Patriarch asked, "What is it that pervades the sands of the world?
(Zhengxian) bowed once and recited the Buddha’s name once. The Patriarch asked, "How does it arise from mastery? (Zhengxian) joined his palms and returned to his original position. The Patriarch—

He immediately granted his seal of approval. "Sustain yourself well; you shall surely inherit your celestial endowment. He further entrusted him with this verse: "The compassionate pointing of Vulture Peak is the heart-mind of the ancient Buddhas;

Transmitted through successive generations down to the present day. Entrust this to the gifted one; let it be held in high esteem. The time has come to continue the flame and illuminate the ancestral hall."
Sengzheng Tai’s dharma name was Hongyin. He was the son of the Zhang family of Longtai in Min County. By nature he was compassionate and kind, and his innate wisdom flourished from within.

Having lost both parents at an early age, he possessed a resolute will from his youth. Remembering his filial piety toward his stern and loving parents, whose kindness was boundless, he resolved his mind upon the observance of the precepts and looked upward to invoke the holy and true ones, vowing that his parents might be liberated from suffering and swiftly transcend to the celestial realms. With such fervor, he set his heart on renunciation.

Dunwang went to Gaoguan and devoted himself to Chan Master Tianzhang, where he was instructed in the precepts and studied Bodhi. He diligently researched the Mahāyāna, thoroughly clarifying both compassion and wisdom.
[He mastered] the efficacious transmission of medicine, the majestic and numinous essentials of the Dharma, and the perfect, sudden, definitive meaning.

One day, he reflected: "The World-Honored One held up a flower; the Patriarch Baizhang pointed directly. (Zhengtai) I must exhaustively investigate this principle, yet I am ashamed that I have not yet attained realization."
He entered. With exceptional devotion, he went into the Patriarch’s chamber, prostrated before the seat, and requested instruction.

The Patriarch saw him and asked, "Who are you? He replied, "I am Zhengtai. The Patriarch said, "Zhengtai is the command of the spring; all things increase their brilliance through the fundamental truth.
He replied, "The numinous clarity manifests the mechanism of transformation; the two truths harmonize to form equal enlightenment. Thereupon, he spoke a verse: [Verse follows]

[The Master] said: "Purity is the primordial spring; it manifests universally, illuminating all things. When the single principle is fully integrated, one is the Buddha of Vast Attainment and Non-action. [Zu] said: "Spring has arrived.
(Zhengtai) assumed a compassionate countenance with a joyful expression, stepped forward, and offered his greetings. [Zu] asked: "What is the Buddha of Non-action?
(Tai) pressed his palms together at his chest and returned to his original position. The Master certified him as being thus. "You should preserve this well."

"Entrust this to you. Until it reaches the state of true purity, you shall succeed to the Imperial Edicts. He further entrusted him with a verse: 'A single flower on Mount Shaoshi has blossomed into five petals;

The succession of fragrance shall not cease until a worthy talent appears. I entrust to you the cultivation of pure and wondrous truth; The time has come to continue the glory of the Patriarchal Hall.'"
This person, whose name is Foten (lit. "Fruit Ascends") and whose courtesy name is Shaoquan, is the son of Huang, a thousand-man commander from Wanan in Fuzhou.

By nature he is benevolent and virtuous, and in his resolve he is upright and sincere. He contemplates the boundless kindness of his parents and feels ashamed that he has failed to repay it with the devotion due to a filial son.

Sinking his heart and purifying his thoughts, he observed the fasts with sincere devotion. Taking refuge in the Benevolent One and placing faith in the Dharma and the Sangha, he looked up to the Triple Gem with compassion and prayed that his parents might attain transcendence.
Seeing that this floating world is not solid, he emerged from the toil of worldly existence to study the Way.
He read and recited the Mahāyāna sūtras and investigated their profound mysteries. He cultivated the six perfections to perfection and abruptly cast off the four torrents of saṃsāra.

Yet, though he aspired to the unsurpassed style of the Dharma, he had not yet reached its subtle purport. One day, with sincere devotion, he respectfully entered the master’s chamber and hastened before his seat to prostrate.
The Master saw him and asked, "Who is this? He replied, "This is Guoteng. The Master said, "Guoteng wanders through the Dharma-realm;

whether you drift or sink depends on yourself—you should observe this for yourself. He replied, "Through the Prajñāpāramitā I enter the ocean of enlightenment; my perfect cultivation lies within me, manifesting true luminosity.

He then spoke a verse: "Originally, truth is equal and impartial; Its radiance responds throughout the ten directions. Through sudden awakening, the returning light shines back; It is pure and stainless."
The essence and function are complete; the Master’s seal is likewise so. You should cultivate them deeply until you reach the state of true purity. He further entrusted him with this verse:
"A single branch of spring before the cliff of Shaoshi, Its fragrance continues through successive generations unto the Lord of Spring. Entrusted to one who knows the sound, cherish it well."
At this time, following the awakening [of the Dharma], he shall propagate the school’s tradition.
This person, whose formal title is Yuequan, is the son of the Shuai family from Fuqing County. By nature, he is benevolent and compassionate.
He established his mind upon filial piety and righteousness. Seeing that this floating world is not solid, he contemplated the swiftness of impermanence.
Cleansing his heart and purifying his thoughts, he offered his sincerity to the Triple Gem. Resolving to practice the Way, he studied the One Vehicle.

He requested instruction from the Zen Master Tiantong and reverently received the Bodhisattva precepts. One day, he went to visit the Patriarch’s quarters and beheld a multitude of eminent disciples, like dragons and elephants.
They questioned one another, saying, "Our practice does not clarify the nature of the mind; it is not ultimate.

(Zhenggong) reflected on this, feeling ashamed that he had not yet attained awakening, wondering how he could possibly catch up later. With sincere devotion, he entered the Patriarch’s chamber directly and prostrated before his seat.
The Patriarch asked, "What have you been doing? He replied, "I observe the fasts and recite the name of Amitābha. The Patriarch asked, "To what end is your vow? He replied, "From..."
"Upon hearing [the word], one enters samādhi. The Patriarch asked, "Who is it that observes the fast? He replied, "From my very awakening.
The Patriarch said, "From hearing, one enters samādhi—what is the principle behind this? (Zhenggong) bowed once, rose, and placed his palms together at his chest.
After remaining silent for a long while, he presented a verse, saying: "Bodhi arises from the mind; The bright mirror’s light is pure and clear. The wondrous original nature..."
Perfectly accomplished, it penetrates everywhere; the Patriarchal Seal is thus. You should support it well, deeply cultivating and nourishing it until it reaches true purity.
He further entrusted him with a verse: "Entering samādhi through hearing, One personally beholds the Ancient Amitābha. I entrust this to you; you should hold it in reverence.
The time has come for the noble one after awakening."
This is Zheng Yuhao, whose courtesy name is Quan. He is the son of the Wei family of Fucheng County. By nature he is benevolent and wise; his resolve is upright and honest.
His filial conduct is devout and sincere, and he observes the fasts and precepts with diligence.

Wishing for his parents to transcend to the celestial realms, he has resolved his mind upon the profound Way and requested instruction from Chan Master Yuetan, reverently receiving the Bodhisattva precepts. One day, he went...
He visited the Patriarch’s quarters and saw that the various monks were excellent, examining one another with refined speech and possessing a true and clear understanding.
(Zhengyu) felt ashamed and humbled, as he had not yet grasped the Great Meaning. One day, with single-minded sincerity, he entered the quarters.
The Patriarch saw him and asked, "Who are you? He replied, "I am a true son of the Buddha. The Patriarch said, "Whose style have you ever practiced? He replied, "That of heterodoxy."

The Master did not acknowledge him. Nanyue said, "I do not ask about the True Buddha; how is it that you are his son? (Zhengyue) bowed his head once. The Master said, "How is it that you are the True Buddha?

(Zhengyue) made a formal inquiry with hands folded and returned to his place, then presented this verse: The body is the Way, The Way is the body. Without body, there is no Way; Without Way, there is no body. The Way and the body are one; They are neither two nor three. If one wishes to know the Buddha, Look at the form before you.
Prajñā is eternally indestructible; it is like the Tathatā and Avalokiteśvara. Primordially wondrous and perfectly penetrating, it is unobstructed throughout all places.
The Patriarchal Seal is thus; you should maintain it well. Refining that which is deep and hidden until it reaches true, pure, and wondrous perfection, you shall succeed to Tian-dong.
Furthermore, he entrusted him with this verse: "The Patriarchal Lamp continues its flame, stretching from antiquity to the present; in its succession, one should treasure it."
I entrust this to you most earnestly; you must transmit it in succession.
Herein is Guyang, styled Dasheng, the son of the Lin family of Houguan County. He has long cultivated the roots of virtue.

By nature compassionate and kind, he established his mind upon filial piety and righteousness. His resolve was firm and unyielding as he contemplated the profound and incomparable kindness and virtue of his parents.

Realizing that impermanence is swift and that the matter of birth and death is of the utmost gravity, he reflected: "If I do not cultivate my mind, upon what can I rely? Thereupon, he purified his heart through fasting and observance, maintaining sincere faith and devotion.
Relying on the great compassion of the Triple Gem, he vowed that both his parents might attain blessings and goodness, and thus proceeded forward.

Xuanyou had thoroughly penetrated the wondrous Way. He traveled to consult his teachers and seek out friends, resolving the nature of his body and mind. To cease delusion and return to the truth, one must rely upon the Dharma rules.
One day, with exceptional sincerity, he went to seek the Master’s guidance. Upon seeing him, the Master asked, "What is your name? He replied:
Guoyang said, "The fruit shines forth, illuminating the Dharma-realm; through sudden awakening to perfect clarity, one enters the true state of the sages.

He replied, "The true mind responds to all lands and moments; vast, penetrating, empty, and spiritual, it realizes Bodhi. He then spoke this verse: "The nature of the mind is fundamentally empty and spiritual."
Pure and naturally luminous, clearly understood without obstruction, one enters instantaneously the city of Ultimate Bliss. My seal is thus; you should maintain it well until it reaches true purity.
He further entrusted him with a verse: "A single branch from Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa has been sent afar; Only now do I know the *utpala* flower blooms amidst the fire.
I now entrust this to you; you must hold it in deep reverence. The time has come for you to illuminate the ancestors and manifest your realization."
This Guojin, styled Dasheng, was the son of the Zhuo family of Changle County. By nature he was compassionate and gentle; filial, righteous, serene, and tranquil.
He reflected that the kindness of his parents was difficult to repay, yet the assembly of glory and honor suddenly vanished through impermanence.

Enmeshed by the afflictions of attachment, he realized that gain and loss are never fixed. Thereupon, he resolved to observe the fasts and precepts, determined to practice with steadfast intent, hoping that the Triple Gem would bestow its grace.

With vast compassion, I vow that my parents may ascend to the celestial realms. I pledge to study Prajñāpāramitā and advance toward Bodhi, penetrating the true and wondrous, and investigating the profound and subtle.
One day, a virtuous friend and I mutually investigated the direct pointing of the Holy Patriarchs—the transcendent and mysterious Way beyond the categories.

If one does not clarify the mind and perceive the nature, how can one penetrate the essential meaning of the ancestral school? Therefore, with sincere devotion, he respectfully entered the Master’s room, prostrated himself before the seat, and bowed his head.
When the Master saw him, he asked, "Who is it? He replied, "It is Guojin. The Master said, "Guojin moistens the myriad streams; as for the single point that returns to the source, what is it like?
He replied, "The lamp of wisdom shines throughout the ten directions; in a mere instant, the light turns back upon itself."
Entering True Illumination, he spoke this verse: "From the very beginning, causes and conditions manifest the great trichiliocosm;

its tranquil essence is suchness, and reflecting back, one realizes Great Sovereignty. The Master’s seal is likewise so; you should skillfully support it. Deeply excavate the luminous wonder, and further entrust it with another verse:
"A single branch from Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa has been transmitted afar; only now do I know that the *utpala* flower blooms within the fire. I now entrust it to you."
I entrust this to you; it should be treated with due respect. This was written at the time when the ancestral legacy was being illuminated by Master Juehou Cai.
The present subject, named Zhengjing (also styled Chuanquan), is the son of the Yu family of Jianyang County in Jianning Prefecture.

By nature he is upright and honest, compassionate, filial, and righteous. He contemplates the vastness of his parents' kindness and places faith in the profound and subtle Way of the Triple Gem. He maintains a vegetarian fast...
He was observant of the precepts and devout, earnestly preserving the holy path. He drew near to the worthy and chose his friends with care, aspiring toward Bodhi.

He requested instruction from the Chan Master Yuetai, seeking to receive the teachings. One day, he went to visit the Patriarch’s quarters, where he prostrated himself with great reverence and earnestly sought compassionate guidance.
The Patriarch questioned him, saying, "From what region do you come? He replied, "My name and surname are the same as yours. The Patriarch said, "Our lives are shared..."
"There is a difference. He replied, "I merely admire the Mahāyāna. The Patriarch said, "I do not ask about the Mahāyāna;

what is your mind? (Zhengjing) [The monk] picked up a blade of grass. The Patriarch said, "What is this that accords with me? (Zhengjing) [The monk] opened his eyes and stared directly at him, then presented this verse:
"Profound stillness is fundamentally empty and spiritual; Purity is naturally perfect and luminous. Seizing the opportunity, I gather in and nourish the Real."

He emitted a brilliant light; the Patriarchal Seal is likewise so. You should skillfully train and guide [disciples] until they reach the state of true purity. He further entrusted them with a verse: "The Patriarchal Seal is transmitted from one to another;
Those with the karmic affinity shall continue the succession of fragrance. I entrust this to you: you must hold it in high esteem; The time has come to spread the light of the Patriarchs."
